decisions.reason: The source concerns battery-connector access on the integrated board, not the separate power board's USB-C type, data lines, or sourceability.
The battery-connector obstruction on the integrated board does not change the retained mechanical constraints of the former main board.
This candidate already records that the separate power board is absent from the single-board design; the integrated-board connector-access issue does not alter that fact.
The source addresses an integrated-board battery connector near USB-C and does not change the former sensor-board layout or its absence from the single-board design.

Although both Requirements concern a battery connector, this candidate describes the former separate power-board interface, while the source specifically changes accessibility on the integrated board.
Requiring unobstructed battery-connector access does not necessarily change the integrated board's cost, sourcing, or connector-reduction policies.
The battery-connector access issue is unrelated to the display-backlight circuit, supply options, switching, or connector specification.
The source changes mechanical accessibility of the battery connector, not charging behavior, power rails, battery efficiency, or the AXP2101 choice.
Resolving connector access within the integrated layout does not alter the decision to consolidate all functions onto one board.
The source identifies a placement and access problem with an L-shaped connector but does not change the through-hole assembly requirement for connectors.
The battery-connector obstruction does not affect the quantity, type, interface, or purpose of the display light-sensor port.
The source does not change the ESP32 breakout or its 1.27 mm pin-header pitch.
